claims.text: The initial CoCuFeNiPd nanoparticles are homogeneous and equiatomic.
The initial CoCuFeNiPd nanoparticles are crystallized as an FCC solid solution.
A conformal 1–2 nm SiO2 shell can be applied using sol–gel deposition.
An ultrathin SiO2 coating suppresses surface atomic diffusion in equiatomic CoCuFeNiPd nanoparticles.
The SiO2 shell functions as a physical diffusion barrier.
The SiO2 shell modifies the surface energy of the nanoparticles.
Suppressing surface atomic mobility inhibits elemental surface segregation.
Suppressing atomic mobility maintains a balanced elemental distribution and high configurational entropy.
Diffusion-mediated elemental segregation leads to phase separation.
Phase separation causes degradation of catalytic and thermoelectric properties.
SiO2-coated CoCuFeNiPd nanoparticles will retain a uniform solid-solution structure during inert-atmosphere cycling from 473 to 1923 K.
SiO2-coated CoCuFeNiPd nanoparticles will retain stable catalytic properties at temperatures up to 1923 K.
SiO2-coated CoCuFeNiPd nanoparticles will retain stable thermoelectric properties at temperatures up to 1923 K.
Uncoated CoCuFeNiPd nanoparticles will exhibit earlier surface segregation and phase separation than coated nanoparticles under identical thermal conditions.
Uncoated CoCuFeNiPd nanoparticles will undergo greater catalytic and thermoelectric performance deterioration than coated nanoparticles.
The predicted stabilizing effect is conditional on an inert atmosphere.
